sources.title: Memories Supporting Myself: Autobiographical Memory Supports Self-Continuity in Alzheimer's Disease
sources.study_design: empirical study of autobiographical memory and subjective self-continuity in people with mild Alzheimer's disease
limitations: Clinical population and cross-sectional associations limit generalisation.
Subjective self-continuity is a psychological construct and is not equivalent to metaphysical persistence of an individual subject.
Associations between autobiographical memory and self-continuity do not establish that memory is necessary or sufficient for personal identity.

sources.title: Developments in the functions of autobiographical memory: An advanced review
sources.study_design: advanced review of autobiographical-memory functions including self-continuity
limitations: Much supporting literature is correlational and uses self-report measures.
Review-level synthesis does not identify a single necessary neural mechanism for identity.
Psychological self-continuity should not be conflated with post-mortem continuity.

sources.title: Self-Continuity
sources.study_design: review of past-present, present-future and global self-continuity, including psychological, behavioral and neural correlates
limitations: Self-continuity is operationalised as a subjective and psychological relation across temporal selves.
Neural correlates of self-continuity do not settle the ontology of personal identity.
The review does not test consciousness after biological death.

sources.title: Studying death and near-death experiences requires neuroscientific expertise

sources.study_design: review and integrative neuroscientific model of near-death experiences

claims.text: In a clinical study of mild Alzheimer's disease, autobiographical-memory performance was associated with participants' reported sense of self-continuity.
limitations: The result concerns a psychological measure of self-continuity in a clinical population.
claims.uncertainty: The study does not determine whether autobiographical memory is necessary or sufficient for personal identity, nor whether identity can continue after death.

claims.text: Autobiographical memory is widely studied as serving self-continuity alongside directive and social functions, but much of the supporting literature is correlational or self-report based.
limitations: The review explicitly notes limitations of correlational and self-report evidence.
claims.uncertainty: A functional link between memory and self-continuity does not settle what constitutes metaphysical identity.

claims.text: Self-continuity is operationalised in contemporary psychology as a subjective connection among past, present and future selves, with identifiable psychological and neural correlates.
limitations: Subjective self-continuity is not synonymous with numerical identity or post-mortem survival.
claims.uncertainty: Multiple philosophical accounts of personal identity remain compatible with the psychological findings.

claims.text: Near-death research requires careful separation of cardiac arrest, brain death, unresponsiveness and consciousness terminology; imprecise neurological assumptions can invalidate stronger inferences.
limitations: This is methodological criticism, not a prospective test of NDE timing or ontology.
claims.uncertainty: Correcting terminology narrows what can be inferred but does not decide whether consciousness can continue beyond irreversible biological death.

claims.text: A 2025 neuroscientific review proposes that converging neurophysiological processes can account for major features of near-death experiences without treating NDE phenomenology as direct evidence of consciousness outside brain function.
limitations: A proposed model is not equivalent to complete mechanistic proof and does not test every conceivable alternative explanation.
claims.uncertainty: The explanatory adequacy and boundary conditions of the model remain empirical questions.

correction_impact_assessment.basis: The mapped claim concerns the review's broad converging-process model and does not quote or depend on the corrected Box 2 precursor term.

batch_conclusion.statement: Batch 2 strengthens the distinction between psychological self-continuity, autobiographical memory and metaphysical persistence, while adding methodological constraints on NDE inference. The evidence supports strong links between brain-based memory/self processes and experienced continuity under studied conditions, but does not by itself establish either post-mortem survival or its impossibility.
